sanskrit: ity etad bruvato rājan brāhmaṇasya mayā śrutam kathāṃ kathayataḥ puṇyāṃ dharmajñasya purātanīm
english: Thus, O king, I heard this from the brāhmaṇa as he spoke, that knower of dharma reciting the holy and ancient tale.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ cāpi mayā bhūyaḥ kṛṣṇasyāpi viśāṃ pate kathāṃ kathayataḥ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prati pāṇḍava
english: And moreover, O lord of peoples, O Pāṇḍava, I once heard this too from Kṛṣṇa, who long ago recited it concerning a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: evam eva ca māṃ nityaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ saṃdiśanti vai pratiśrutya bhaved deyaṃ nāśā kāryā hi brāhmaṇaiḥ
english: And just so the brāhmaṇas ever instruct me: once a promise is made, the gift must be given; never should the brāhmaṇas' hope be left unfulfilled.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hy āśayā pūrvaṃ kṛtayā pṛthivīpate susamiddho yathā dīptaḥ pāvakas tadvidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: For a brāhmaṇa, O lord of the earth, once his hope has been kindled, is reckoned to be like a well-fed, blazing fire.

sanskrit: yaṃ nirīkṣeta saṃkruddha āśayā pūrvajātayā pradaheta hi taṃ rājan kakṣam akṣayyabhug yathā
english: Whomever he, enraged, fixes his gaze upon—his hope once roused—him, O king, he would consume utterly, as an inexhaustible fire devours dry brushwood.

sanskrit: sa eva hi yadā tuṣṭo vacasā pratinandati bhavaty agadasaṃkāśo viṣaye tasya bhārata
english: Yet that same brāhmaṇa, when contented, gives thanks with his words, and becomes for that man's realm like a healing medicine, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: putrān pautrān paśūṃś caiva bāndhavān sacivāṃs tathā puraṃ janapadaṃ caiva śāntir iṣṭeva puṣyati
english: Sons and grandsons, cattle and kinsmen, ministers too, the city and the countryside—all these he causes to flourish, like a peace devoutly sought.

sanskrit: etad dhi paramaṃ tejo brāhmaṇasyeha dṛśyate sahasrakiraṇasyeva savitur dharaṇītale
english: For this supreme splendor of the brāhmaṇa is seen here on earth, like that of the thousand-rayed Sun upon the face of the world.

sanskrit: tasmād dātavyam eveha pratiśrutya yudhiṣṭhira yadīcchec chobhanāṃ jātiṃ prāptuṃ bharatasattama
english: Therefore, once a promise is made, the gift must indeed be given, Yudhiṣṭhira, if one wishes to attain a fair birth, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya hi dattena dhruvaṃ svargo hy anuttamaḥ śakyaṃ prāptuṃ viśeṣeṇa dānaṃ hi mahatī kriyā
english: For by what is given to a brāhmaṇa, the unsurpassed heaven can surely be won, and won abundantly; for giving is a mighty act.

sanskrit: ito dattena jīvanti devatāḥ pitaras tathā tasmād dānāni deyāni brāhmaṇebhyo vijānatā
english: By what is given here the gods live, and the ancestors likewise; therefore the wise man should bestow his gifts upon the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: mahad dhi bharataśreṣṭha brāhmaṇas tīrtham ucyate velāyāṃ na tu kasyāṃ cid gacched vipro hy apūjitaḥ
english: For the brāhmaṇa, O best of the Bharatas, is called a great holy ford; at no fitting hour should a brāhmaṇa depart unhonored.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mitrasauhṛdabhāvena upadeśaṃ karoti yaḥ jātyāvarasya rājarṣe doṣas tasya bhaven na vā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When one, out of the goodwill of friendship, gives instruction to a man of lower birth, O royal sage—does fault arise for him or not?

sanskrit: etad icchāmi tattvena vyākhyātuṃ vai pitāmaha sūkṣmā gatir hi dharmasya yatra muhyanti mānavāḥ
english: This I wish to have explained in truth, O grandfather; for subtle is the course of dharma, wherein men go astray.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi śṛṇu rājan yathāgamam ṛṣīṇāṃ vadatāṃ pūrvaṃ śrutam āsīd yathā mayā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you, O king; listen as it has come down to us, even as I heard it long ago from the speech of the sages.

sanskrit: upadeśo na kartavyo jātihīnasya kasya cit upadeśe mahān doṣa upādhyāyasya bhāṣyate
english: Instruction should not be given to any man of base birth; a grave fault is declared to fall upon the teacher for such instruction.

sanskrit: nidarśanam idaṃ rājañ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha duruktavacane rājan yathā pūrvaṃ yudhiṣṭhira brahmāśramapade vṛttaṃ pārśve himavataḥ śubhe
english: Hear from me this illustration, O king, O bull of the Bharatas—of the offense of ill-spoken words, Yudhiṣṭhira—of what came to pass of old at a brahmanic hermitage upon the fair flank of the Himavat.

sanskrit: tatrāśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ nānāvṛkṣagaṇāyutam bahugulmalatākīrṇaṃ mṛgadvijaniṣevitam
english: There stood a holy hermitage, set amid clusters of many kinds of trees, thick with shrubs and creepers, frequented by deer and birds.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇasaṃghuṣṭaṃ ramyaṃ puṣpitakānanam vratibhir bahubhiḥ kīrṇaṃ tāpasair upaśobhitam
english: Resounding with siddhas and cāraṇas, lovely, its groves in flower, thronged with many keepers of vows and graced by ascetics.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiś ca mahābhāgaiḥ sūryajvalanasaṃnibhaiḥ niyamavratasaṃpannaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ tapasvibhiḥ dīkṣitair bharataśreṣṭha yatāhāraiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Crowded too with brāhmaṇas of great fortune, resplendent as the sun and fire, perfect in restraints and vows—with ascetics, O best of the Bharatas, consecrated, sparing in food, their selves perfected.

sanskrit: vedādhyayanaghoṣaiś ca nāditaṃ bharatarṣabha vālakhilyaiś ca bahubhir yatibhiś ca niṣevitam
english: Filled with the murmur of Vedic recitation, O bull of the Bharatas, and frequented by many Vālakhilyas and by men of strict discipline.

sanskrit: tatra kaś cit samutsāhaṃ kṛtvā śūdro dayānvitaḥ āgato hy āśramapadaṃ pūjitaś ca tapasvibhiḥ
english: There a certain śūdra, summoning his resolve, full of compassion, came to that hermitage and was honored by the ascetics.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā munigaṇān devakalpān mahaujasaḥ vahato vividhā dīkṣāḥ saṃprahṛṣyata bhārata
english: And seeing those hosts of sages, godlike and of great might, bearing their manifold vows, he was filled with joy, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāsya buddhir abhavat tapasye bharatarṣabha tato 'bravīt kulapatiṃ pādau saṃgṛhya bhārata
english: Then his mind turned toward asceticism, O bull of the Bharatas; and so, clasping his feet, he addressed the head of the community, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād icchāmi dharmaṃ cartuṃ dvijarṣabha tan māṃ tvaṃ bhagavan vaktuṃ pravrājayitum arhasi
english: By your grace I wish to practice dharma, O bull among the twice-born; therefore, O blessed one, you ought to instruct me and to set me upon the ascetic's path.

sanskrit: varṇāvaro 'haṃ bhagavañ śūdro jātyāsmi sattama śuśrūṣāṃ kartum icchāmi prapannāya prasīda me
english: I am of a lower order, O blessed one—a śūdra by birth, O most excellent; I wish to render service. Be gracious to me, who have come to you for refuge.

sanskrit: kulapatir uvāca na śakyam iha śūdreṇa liṅgam āśritya vartitum āsyatāṃ yadi te buddhiḥ śuśrūṣānirato bhava
english: The head of the community said: It is not possible here for a śūdra to live having taken up the ascetic's emblem. Stay, if such is your mind, and devote yourself to service.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktas tu muninā sa śūdro 'cintayan nṛpa katham atra mayā kāryaṃ śraddhā dharme parā ca me vijñātam evaṃ bhavatu kariṣye priyam ātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by the sage, that śūdra reflected, O king: "What am I to do in this? My faith in dharma is supreme. So be it—I shall do what is dear to my own soul."

sanskrit: gatvāśramapadād dūram uṭajaṃ kṛtavāṃs tu saḥ tatra vediṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca devatāyatanāni ca niveśya bharataśreṣṭha niyamastho 'bhavat sukham
english: Going far from the hermitage, he built himself a hut of leaves; and there, having set in place an altar, a hallowed ground, and shrines for the deities, O best of the Bharatas, he abode happily, firm in his vows.

sanskrit: abhiṣekāṃś ca niyamān devatāyataneṣu ca baliṃ ca kṛtvā hutvā ca devatāṃ cāpy apūjayat
english: Performing ablutions and observances, and offering the bali-oblation at the shrines, and pouring oblations into the fire, he worshiped the deities as well.

sanskrit: saṃkalpaniyamopetaḥ phalāhāro jitendriyaḥ nityaṃ saṃnihitābhiś ca oṣadhībhiḥ phalais tathā
english: Endowed with resolve and restraint, living on fruit, his senses subdued, ever furnished with the herbs and fruits that lay close at hand.

sanskrit: atithīn pūjayām āsa yathāvat samupāgatān evaṃ hi sumahān kālo vyatyakrāmat sa tasya vai
english: He honored, in due form, the guests who came to him; and thus a very long span of time passed by for him.

sanskrit: athāsya munir āgacchat saṃgatyā vai tam āśramam saṃpūjya svāgatenarṣiṃ vidhivat paryatoṣayat
english: Then a sage came by chance to his hermitage; and welcoming the seer with words of greeting, he gratified him fully according to rule.

sanskrit: anukūlāḥ kathāḥ kṛtvā yathāvat paryapṛcchata ṛṣiḥ paramatejasvī dharmātmā saṃyatendriyaḥ
english: Having exchanged agreeable converse, the seer—of supreme splendor, righteous of soul, his senses controlled—questioned him duly.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bahuśas tasya śūdrasya bharatarṣabha so 'gacchad āśramam ṛṣiḥ śūdraṃ draṣṭuṃ nararṣabha
english: Thus, O bull of the Bharatas, that seer went many times to the śūdra's hermitage, O bull among men, to see the śūdra.

sanskrit: atha taṃ tāpasaṃ śūdraḥ so 'bravīd bharatarṣabha pitṛkāryaṃ kariṣyāmi tatra me 'nugrahaṃ kuru
english: Then the śūdra said to that ascetic, O bull of the Bharatas: "I shall perform a rite for the ancestors; in this grant me your favor."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva taṃ vipra uvāca bharatarṣabha śucir bhūtvā sa śūdras tu tasyarṣeḥ pādyam ānayat
english: "So be it," the brāhmaṇa said to him, O bull of the Bharatas; and the śūdra, having purified himself, brought water for that seer's feet.

sanskrit: atha darbhāṃś ca vanyāś ca oṣadhīr bharatarṣabha pavitram āsanaṃ caiva bṛsīṃ ca samupānayat
english: Then darbha grass and wild herbs, O bull of the Bharatas, and a purifying strainer, a seat, and a grass cushion he brought near.

sanskrit: atha dakṣiṇam āvṛtya bṛsīṃ paramaśīrṣikām kṛtām anyāyato dṛṣṭvā tatas tam ṛṣir abravīt
english: Then, turning it to the south, when the seer saw the cushion's head laid out the wrong way, contrary to rule, he spoke to him.

sanskrit: kuruṣvaitāṃ pūrvaśīrṣāṃ bhava codaṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ sa ca tat kṛtavāñ śūdraḥ sarvaṃ yad ṛṣir abravīt
english: "Set its head toward the east, and face the north, being purified." And the śūdra did all that the seer had told him.

sanskrit: yathopadiṣṭaṃ medhāvī darbhādīṃs tān yathātatham havyakavyavidhiṃ kṛtsnam uktaṃ tena tapasvinā
english: As instructed, the discerning man arranged the darbha grass and the rest just so; and the whole rule of offerings to gods and ancestors was told to him by that ascetic.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṇā pitṛkārye ca sa ca dharmapathe sthitaḥ pitṛkārye kṛte cāpi visṛṣṭaḥ sa jagāma ha
english: By the seer he was thus guided in the rite for the ancestors, and he himself stayed firm upon the path of dharma; and when the rite was done, the seer, taking his leave, departed.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya sa tapyañ śūdratāpasaḥ vane pañcatvam agamat sukṛtena ca tena vai ajāyata mahārājarājavaṃśe mahādyutiḥ
english: Then after a long time that śūdra-ascetic, performing his austerities, met dissolution in the forest; and by that good deed he was reborn, of great radiance, O great king, in a royal lineage of kings.

sanskrit: tathaiva sa ṛṣis tāta kāladharmam avāpya ha purohitakule vipra ājāto bharatarṣabha
english: And likewise that seer, my child, having met his appointed end, was reborn as a brāhmaṇa in the family of a royal chaplain, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau tatra saṃbhūtāv ubhau śūdramunī tadā krameṇa vardhitau cāpi vidyāsu kuśalāv ubhau
english: Thus the two of them—the śūdra and the sage—were both born there; and growing up in due course, both became skilled in the branches of learning.

sanskrit: atharvavede vede ca babhūvarṣiḥ suniścitaḥ kalpaprayoge cotpanne jyotiṣe ca paraṃ gataḥ sakhye cāpi parā prītis tayoś cāpi vyavardhata
english: In the Atharvaveda and the other Veda the seer became well-grounded, accomplished in the practice of ritual and in astronomy he attained the highest mastery; and between the two of them a supreme delight in friendship grew apace.

sanskrit: pitary uparate cāpi kṛtaśaucaḥ sa bhārata abhiṣiktaḥ prakṛtibhī rājaputraḥ sa pārthivaḥ abhiṣiktena sa ṛṣir abhiṣiktaḥ purohitaḥ
english: And when his father had passed away, the prince, having completed the rites of purification, O Bhārata, was anointed king by the subjects; and by the anointed king that seer was anointed as chaplain.

sanskrit: sa taṃ purodhāya sukham avasad bharatarṣabha rājyaṃ śaśāsa dharmeṇa prajāś ca paripālayan
english: Placing him at his head, the king dwelt happily, O bull of the Bharatas, ruling his kingdom by dharma and guarding his subjects well.

sanskrit: puṇyāhavācane nityaṃ dharmakāryeṣu cāsakṛt utsmayan prāhasac cāpi dṛṣṭvā rājā purohitam evaṃ sa bahuśo rājan purodhasam upāhasat
english: At the proclaiming of auspicious days, and repeatedly in the rites of dharma, the king, on seeing the chaplain, would smile and even laugh; and thus, O king, many times did he laugh at the chaplain.

sanskrit: lakṣayitvā purodhās tu bahuśastaṃ narādhipam utsmayantaṃ ca satataṃ dṛṣṭvāsau manyumān abhūt
english: But the chaplain, having marked the lord of men do so many times, and seeing him forever smiling, grew filled with resentment.

sanskrit: atha śūnye purodhās tu saha rājñā samāgataḥ kathābhir anukūlābhī rājānam abhirāmayat
english: Then in a solitary place the chaplain, meeting with the king, delighted him with agreeable conversation.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn narendraṃ sa purodhā bharatarṣabha varam icchāmy ahaṃ tv ekaṃ tvayā dattaṃ mahādyute
english: Then that chaplain said to the lord of men, O bull of the Bharatas: "One boon I desire, to be granted by you, O greatly radiant one."

sanskrit: rājovāca varāṇāṃ te śataṃ dadyāṃ kim utaikaṃ dvijottama snehāc ca bahumānāc ca nāsty adeyaṃ hi me tava
english: The king said: A hundred boons would I grant you, how much more a single one, O best of the twice-born; for out of affection and high regard there is nothing I would withhold from you.

sanskrit: purohita uvāca ekaṃ vai varam icchāmi yadi tuṣṭo 'si pārthiva yad dadāsi mahārāja satyaṃ tad vada mānṛtam
english: The chaplain said: One boon indeed I desire, if you are pleased, O lord of the earth; what you grant, O great king, speak it truly, and let it be no falsehood.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca bāḍham ity eva taṃ rājā pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhira yadi jñāsyāmi vakṣyāmi ajānan na tu saṃvade
english: Bhīṣma said: "So be it," the king replied to him, O Yudhiṣṭhira; "if I shall know the answer, I will tell it; but not knowing, I will not speak."

sanskrit: purohita uvāca puṇyāhavācane nityaṃ dharmakṛtyeṣu cāsakṛt śāntihomeṣu ca sadā kiṃ tvaṃ hasasi vīkṣya mām
english: The chaplain said: At the proclaiming of auspicious days, ever in the rites of dharma, and always at the homas for peace—why is it that, looking upon me, you laugh?

sanskrit: savrīḍaṃ vai bhavati hi mano me hasatā tvayā kāmayā śāpito rājan nānyathā vaktum arhasi
english: My mind is filled with shame at your laughing; adjured by my wish, O king, you ought not to speak otherwise than the truth.

sanskrit: bhāvyaṃ hi kāraṇenātra na te hāsyam akāraṇam kautūhalaṃ me subhṛśaṃ tattvena kathayasva me
english: There must surely be a cause in this; your laughter is not without reason. My curiosity is very keen—tell me the truth of it.

sanskrit: rājovāca evam ukte tvayā vipra yad avācyaṃ bhaved api avaśyam eva vaktavyaṃ śṛṇuṣvaikamanā dvija
english: The king said: Since you have spoken thus, O brāhmaṇa, even what ought not to be told must now of necessity be told. Listen with single mind, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: pūrvadehe yathā vṛttaṃ tan nibodha dvijottama jātiṃ smarāmy ahaṃ brahmann avadhānena me śṛṇu
english: Learn what came to pass in a former body, O best of the twice-born; I remember my birth, O brāhmaṇa—listen to me attentively.

sanskrit: śūdro 'ham abhavaṃ pūrvaṃ tāpaso bhṛśasaṃyutaḥ ṛṣir ugratapās tvaṃ ca tadābhūr dvijasattama
english: A śūdra I was of old, an ascetic strictly self-disciplined; and you, O most excellent of the twice-born, were then a seer of fierce austerity.

sanskrit: prīyatā hi tadā brahman mamānugrahabuddhinā pitṛkārye tvayā pūrvam upadeśaḥ kṛto 'nagha bṛsyāṃ darbheṣu havye ca kavye ca munisattama
english: For then, O brāhmaṇa, out of love and a mind to favor me, you of old gave me instruction in the rite for the ancestors, O sinless one—concerning the grass cushion, the darbha grass, the offering to the gods and the offering to the ancestors, O best of sages.

sanskrit: etena karmadoṣeṇa purodhās tvam ajāyathāḥ ahaṃ rājā ca viprendra paśya kālasya paryayam matkṛte hy upadeśena tvayā prāptam idaṃ phalam
english: By this fault of action you were born a chaplain, and I a king, O chief of brāhmaṇas; behold the turning of time! For through the instruction you gave on my account, this fruit has fallen to you.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād brahman prahase tvāṃ dvijottama na tvāṃ paribhavan brahman prahasāmi gurur bhavān
english: For this reason, O brāhmaṇa, I laugh at you, O best of the twice-born; not in scorn of you do I laugh, O brāhmaṇa—you are my elder.

sanskrit: viparyayeṇa me manyus tena saṃtapyate manaḥ jātiṃ smarāmy ahaṃ tubhyam atas tvāṃ prahasāmi vai
english: At this reversal my heart is grieved, and my mind is sorely pained thereby. I remember our births—for you—and therefore it is that I laugh.

sanskrit: evaṃ tavograṃ hi tapa upadeśena nāśitam purohitatvam utsṛjya yatasva tvaṃ punarbhave
english: Thus your fierce austerity was undone by the giving of instruction; cast off the office of chaplain and strive again toward a future birth.

sanskrit: itas tvam adhamām anyāṃ mā yoniṃ prāpsyase dvija gṛhyatāṃ draviṇaṃ vipra pūtātmā bhava sattama
english: Lest from here you fall into another, baser womb, O twice-born; take this wealth, O brāhmaṇa, and become purified in soul, O excellent one.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato visṛṣṭo rājñā tu vipro dānāny anekaśaḥ brāhmaṇebhyo dadau vittaṃ bhūmiṃ grāmāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, dismissed by the king, the brāhmaṇa bestowed gifts of many kinds—wealth, land, and villages—upon the brāhmaṇas in every way.

sanskrit: kṛcchrāṇi cīrtvā ca tato yathoktāni dvijottamaḥ tīrthāni cābhigatvā vai dānāni vividhāni ca
english: And that best of the twice-born, having performed the penances as prescribed, and having visited the holy fords, and made manifold gifts—

sanskrit: dattvā gāś caiva viprāṇāṃ pūtātmā so 'bhavad dvijaḥ tam eva cāśramaṃ gatvā cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ
english: and having given cattle to the brāhmaṇas, that twice-born one became purified in soul; and going back to that very hermitage, he practiced abundant austerity.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhiṃ parāṃ prāpto brāhmaṇo rājasattama saṃmataś cābhavat teṣām āśrame ''śramavāsinām
english: Then the brāhmaṇa attained supreme perfection, O best of kings, and became honored among those dwellers of the hermitage.

sanskrit: evaṃ prāpto mahat kṛcchram ṛṣiḥ sa nṛpasattama brāhmaṇena na vaktavyaṃ tasmād varṇāvare jane
english: Thus that seer came to great distress, O best of kings; therefore a brāhmaṇa should not speak instruction to a person of lower order.

sanskrit: varjayed upadeśaṃ ca sadaiva brāhmaṇo nṛpa upadeśaṃ hi kurvāṇo dvijaḥ kṛcchram avāpnuyāt
english: A brāhmaṇa should ever shun the giving of such instruction, O king; for in giving instruction the twice-born one would come to distress.

sanskrit: eṣitavyaṃ sadā vācā nṛpeṇa dvijasattamāt na pravaktavyam iha hi kiṃ cid varṇāvare jane
english: The king should ever seek knowledge by his speech from the best of the twice-born; but to a person of lower order nothing whatever should here be expounded.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyās trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ eteṣu kathayan rājan brāhmaṇo na praduṣyati
english: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas—these three orders are the twice-born; speaking among these, O king, a brāhmaṇa incurs no fault.

sanskrit: tasmāt sadbhir na vaktavyaṃ kasya cit kiṃ cid agrataḥ sūkṣmā gatir hi dharmasya durjñeyā hy akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Therefore the good should not speak anything in the presence of anyone heedlessly; for subtle is the course of dharma, hard to discern by those whose souls are unperfected.

sanskrit: tasmān maunāni munayo dīkṣāṃ kurvanti cādṛtāḥ duruktasya bhayād rājan nānubhāṣanti kiṃ cana
english: For this reason the sages, with reverence, undertake vows of silence; from fear of ill-spoken words, O king, they answer nothing at all.

sanskrit: dhārmikā guṇasaṃpannāḥ satyārjavaparāyaṇāḥ duruktavācābhihatāḥ prāpnuvantīha duṣkṛtam
english: The righteous, endowed with virtues, devoted to truth and uprightness, when stricken by an ill-spoken word, come thereby to evil-doing here.

sanskrit: upadeśo na kartavyaḥ kadā cid api kasya cit upadeśād dhi tat pāpaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ samavāpnuyāt
english: Instruction should never be given at any time to anyone; for from instruction a brāhmaṇa would incur that sin.

sanskrit: vimṛśya tasmāt prājñena vaktavyaṃ dharmam icchatā satyānṛtena hi kṛta upadeśo hinasti vai
english: Therefore the wise man who desires dharma should speak only after reflection; for instruction given through truth mixed with falsehood surely brings harm.
